title: Separate September DMI slopes gave no clear added winter forecast skill in 1981-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether separate slopes for positive and negative September Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI) improve winter DMI forecasts. Each fit used earlier origin years from 1950. The baseline used September DMI, September Nino 3.4 and a time trend. Adding absolute DMI reduced mean squared error by 9.34% in 44 origins from 1981 to 2024. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -24.82% to +31.70%. RMSE fell from 0.20892 to 0.19892 degrees C. All planned check intervals included zero. Using autumn means instead of September gave a 0.02% reduction. This gives no clear added skill under the tested models. It does not show equal skill or rule out physical asymmetry. The question follows prior analyses of the same record, so the test is not an untouched holdout. A short record, revised products, simple models and conditional uncertainty limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and independent numerical checks are included. External records and derived record-level tables remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Separate DMI slopes gave no clear added winter forecast skill. Points show error reduction. Lines show conditional 95% intervals. All intervals include zero. Checks share observations.

citations.reason: Prior descriptive slope test motivated this forecast test. We reuse its named source snapshots and write new code. Data overlap is complete.
